meta.name: Dragons Alliance Premium
meta.description: Restrained-luxury dark UI for Chișinău Delivery — deep navy substrate, brushed-gold primary metal, amethyst crystal secondary jewel, red CTA/danger accent, Playfair Display serif wordmark over Geist sans body. Crystalline glass cards, faceted rim-light, gold hairline shimmer sweeps and WAAPI arrival reveals — all CSS/SVG/WAAPI, zero WebGL.
source_references: docs monogram palette: deep navy #0a0a14/#0d0d1f, brushed gold #b8860b→#d4af37→#f5c542→#fff3c4, amethyst #6d28d9→#7c3aed→#a855f7→#c084fc, red #e94560/#c73050

primary.role: CTA fill, danger/reject accent, primary brand red (the courier/customer surfaces' main action color; text/badge use reads at >=4.5:1 on the dark background — buttons must use primary-dark instead)

secondary.role: brushed-gold metal — brand wordmark ('Dragons'), CTAs on the restaurant-partner premium surface, crests, live shimmer sweeps, key numeric values (earnings, prices)

accent.role: amethyst crystal jewel — secondary/live-state accent: realtime pulse dots, glow highlights, secondary CTA (pg-cta-amethyst), 'listening' indicators

neutral.usage: near-black navy substrate stack (0a0a14 deepest → 1e1e35 elevated card) for all backgrounds/surfaces; white only for foreground text, stepped down via opacity (white/10 … white/90) for all secondary/tertiary text and hairline borders instead of a separate grey scale

color.contrast_strategy: dark-on-light inverted — pure dark-mode app (color-scheme: dark forced in :root so native form controls stay dark too); white text at stepped opacity for hierarchy, gold/amethyst reserved for brand and state, CTA fills always use primary-dark (#c73050, 5.29:1) not primary itself (3.83:1) to clear WCAG AA on white text

font_families.heading: 'Playfair Display', Georgia, serif — brand wordmark ('Dragons'), page H1s, crest strip, gold headline numerals
font_families.body: Geist, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif — all UI copy, nav, forms, cards
font_families.mono: Geist Mono — order IDs, timestamps, technical/debug strings only

typography.font_style_notes: high-contrast luxury display serif (Playfair Display) paired with a clean geometric-humanist sans (Geist) — the serif is used sparingly and only for brand-weight moments (wordmark, section H1, big earnings numerals), never body copy; overline tracking is unusually wide (0.28em, seen on .pg-crest-mark) to read as an engraved crest label

spacing.section_rhythm: generous top-level rhythm (mt-16 between footer and content, gap-8 grid rows) contracted to tight rhythm inside cards (gap-2/gap-3, px-4 py-2 on the crest strip) — density increases the deeper you nest

layout.grid_system: single-column content flow inside a centered max-width shell; CSS grid only for footer link columns (sm:grid-cols-3) and dashboard tile rows
layout.max_content_width: max-w-5xl (64rem) is the dominant shell width across customer header/footer/restaurant crest; max-w-3xl for reading-width legal/marketing text; max-w-md/max-w-sm for auth/modal-scale forms
layout.alignment_tendency: centered shell, left-aligned content and text — nav/footer items use flex-wrap with justify-between at the shell level, strict left alignment within

border_radius.pill: 9999px (rounded-full) — avatars, status dots, badge pills, the live-indicator dot — the single most-used radius token in the codebase (201 occurrences)

shape.border_usage: subtle 1px hairlines at low white-opacity (border-white/10 dominant, border-white/5 for barely-there separators, border-white/15 for slightly firmer emphasis) — never a bold/heavy border; premium surfaces swap the hairline color to var(--pg-gold-line) / var(--pg-amethyst-line)
shape.divider_style: 1px hairline, color-tinted by context — plain white/10 on standard surfaces, gold or amethyst gradient-fading-to-transparent hairline (.pg-crest::after, pg-divider-gold/amethyst) on premium/restaurant surfaces

elevation.shadow_style: soft diffused, dark and negative-spread (shadows are near-black with large negative spread, e.g. 0 18px 40px -28px rgba(0,0,0,0.9)) rather than colored ambient light except on gold/amethyst glow states

levels.high: 0 26px 50px -26px rgba(0,0,0,0.95) with a 1px gold-line ring on hover-elevated cards

elevation.depth_cues: layered gradients + blur/glass (backdrop-filter: blur(6px) on .pg-card) + inset top-edge rim-light rather than pure box-shadow; state (new/live) communicated by animated gold/amethyst glow instead of elevation change

iconography.style: outline/filled hybrid inline SVG, hand-authored (no icon library — repo forbids new npm deps)
iconography.stroke_weight: n/a for filled marks (fill=currentColor paths, e.g. the location pin in the customer header); line icons where used follow a ~1.5px stroke
iconography.size_scale: h-4 w-4 (1rem) inline-with-text icons up to h-6 w-6 for standalone action icons
iconography.preferred_set: none — bespoke inline SVG per use, currentColor-tinted so it inherits text-primary/text-gold contextually

motion.easing: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) — a single soft-decel 'arrival' ease shared by every entrance/hover transition (--pg-ease)
motion.entrance_pattern: rise + fade + faint scale-in (translate3d(0,14px,0) scale(0.985) → identity), transform+opacity only for compositor-only 60fps, staggered via delay = index * 60ms for lists
motion.exit_pattern: no dedicated exit choreography observed — elements are removed/replaced by Next.js navigation rather than animated out
motion.philosophy: minimal functional at the interaction layer (snappy 180ms hover), cinematic at the ambient layer (slow multi-second gold/amethyst breathing glows and glints) — motion is restrained and purposeful, never decorative-only, and every animation/transition is stripped under prefers-reduced-motion leaving only the static color/gradient/glass treatment

components.button_style: solid-fill primary (bg-primary-dark, white text) for standard surfaces; on the premium restaurant surface, gold-gradient metallic CTA (.pg-cta: var(--pg-gold-grad) fill, dark #241a02 text, diagonal shimmer sweep overlay, -1px translateY + brightness(1.06) on hover) with an amethyst-gradient secondary variant (.pg-cta-amethyst); rounded-xl, font-semibold/bold, disabled = opacity 0.5
components.input_style: dark filled field (bg matching surface/card tone), 1px white/10-15 border, rounded-xl, no visible focus ring pattern beyond browser default (color-scheme:dark forces native controls dark too)
components.card_style: glass/gradient hybrid — two-layer linear-gradient background (subtle top-lit sheen + navy base wash), 1px hairline ring via box-shadow (not border), backdrop-filter blur(6px), rounded-2xl, inset top rim-light pseudo-element masked to the top ~30%; hover lifts translateY(-2px) and swaps the ring to gold
components.navigation_pattern: sticky top header, backdrop-blur over translucent navy (bg-[#0a0a14]/95), horizontally-scrollable no-scrollbar row on admin surfaces, flat text links with hover:text-white/hover:text-gold, role-gated route groups ((customer)/(courier)/(admin)) each render their own header/nav shell
components.modal_style: not a distinct pattern in this codebase — repo rule explicitly forbids window.confirm; destructive/confirm actions render as inline card-embedded confirmation states rather than a portal/dialog overlay
components.list_style: card-per-row lists (each row = a .pg-card or plain bordered rounded-2xl panel) wrapped in <PremiumReveal as="li" delay={i*60}> for staggered arrival, rather than dense table rows
components.component_notes: the same visual language runs in two registers: a 'standard' register (globals.css tokens: navy/red/gold-orange, used on customer/courier/marketing surfaces) and a 'premium' register (premium.css pg-* tokens: deeper navy + brushed-gold + amethyst crystal, used on the restaurant partner surface) — the premium register is the aspirational target this DNA should be pulled toward platform-wide

aesthetic.visual_metaphor: a jeweled dragon crest catching torchlight — faceted crystal surfaces, brushed metal, gemstone glow
aesthetic.era_influence: contemporary dark-mode SaaS premium (2024-2026 fintech/luxury-app aesthetic) crossed with heraldic/crest motifs (crest strip, wordmark tracking, gold/jewel palette)
aesthetic.genre: luxury editorial meets operational dashboard — restrained fine-dining branding applied to a logistics/delivery product
personality_traits: a little theatrical at rest, disciplined in motion

visual_language.ornamentation: subtle accents — gold hairlines, faceted glints, dragon-scale dot-lattice texture — decorative but never busy; ornamentation concentrates on brand/state moments (crest, new-order glow) and stays absent from dense data surfaces (tables, forms)
visual_language.whitespace_usage: generous at the shell level (max-w-5xl centered, mt-16 section breaks), tightened inside functional clusters (cards, KPI tiles) to keep operational density readable
visual_language.visual_weight_distribution: dark base carries near-zero visual weight so gold/amethyst/red accents read as the only 'loud' elements — weight is concentrated in a handful of brand/CTA/status touches per screen, not spread evenly
visual_language.focal_strategy: single hero element per section (crest wordmark, primary CTA, or the 'new order' glowing card) with everything else receding into the navy field
visual_language.contrast_level: high for accent-vs-background (gold/amethyst/red on near-black), low/subtle for structure (hairline borders, stepped white-opacity text) — contrast is spent deliberately on meaning (brand, state, CTA), not on decoration
visual_language.texture_usage: faint dragon-scale dot-lattice (two offset radial-gradient dot fields, masked to fade top-to-bottom) as an ambient background texture on premium surfaces only; standard surfaces stay flat

composition.hierarchy_method: color weight + typographic hierarchy — gold/serif marks the top of the hierarchy, white-opacity steps (90/80/70/60/50/45/40/35/30/25/20) do the rest without changing scale much
composition.balance_type: asymmetric within a symmetric shell — the outer shell (header/footer/max-w container) is centered and balanced, but content inside (crest wordmark left, live indicator right; card internals) is deliberately asymmetric
composition.flow_direction: top-to-bottom single-column scroll, left-to-right reading within rows
composition.grouping_strategy: card/panel boundaries (glass background + hairline ring) group related data; color (gold vs amethyst vs red) groups by semantic role (brand/value vs live/secondary vs danger/CTA) across the whole app
composition.negative_space_role: negative space is the dominant surface — the deep navy field is treated as active 'space' (with its own ambient gradient glow and texture) rather than empty background, letting a small number of jeweled elements read as precious

imagery.photo_treatment: menu/restaurant photos are presented in clean rounded-xl/2xl frames with no filter overlay; a mandatory-photo gate exists for menu items (conversion lever) but the treatment itself is neutral/realistic, not stylized
imagery.illustration_style: no illustration system — bespoke inline SVG icons only (pins, simple glyphs), no character illustration or spot-illustration library
imagery.graphic_elements: gold/amethyst gradient hairlines, faceted glint sweeps, dragon-scale dot-lattice texture, radial rim-light glows positioned at screen corners
imagery.pattern_usage: one recurring background pattern (dragon-scale dot lattice, 44px tile, two offset layers) used sparingly as an ambient texture, masked to fade rather than tile edge-to-edge
imagery.image_shape: rounded rectangles (rounded-xl/2xl) for photos and cards; rounded-full exclusively for avatars/badges/status dots — no free-form or clipped shapes

interaction_feel.feedback_style: color + motion combined — hover lifts (translateY) paired with a brightness/shadow shift, live/realtime state signaled by a breathing amethyst dot plus a 'Live' label rather than a toast
interaction_feel.hover_behavior: buttons: -1px lift + brightness(1.06) + deeper shadow; cards: -2px lift + hairline ring swaps from white/gold-tinted to solid gold; links: plain color transition (hover:text-white / hover:text-gold), no underline animation
interaction_feel.transition_personality: smooth glide — soft-decel custom easing everywhere, never bouncy/elastic, never abrupt/snappy at the ambient layer though micro-interactions (180ms button hover) do read as brisk
interaction_feel.loading_style: shimmer sweep (diagonal gold sheen crossing a bar/chip, .pg-shimmer) for in-progress/ready states rather than a spinner; realtime freshness shown via a small pulsing amethyst dot, not a skeleton screen system
interaction_feel.microinteraction_density: moderate — reserved for entrance (arrival reveal), hover (lift/shimmer), and live-state (pulse/glint) moments; dense data areas (tables, forms) carry none

brand_voice_in_ui.tone: warm and precise, quietly confident — Romanian-language copy that's direct without being cold ('Cerere trimisă ✓', 'Câștiguri')
brand_voice_in_ui.formality: semi-formal — professional but approachable, second-person informal Romanian, no corporate jargon
brand_voice_in_ui.cta_style: direct imperative kept short ('Devino partener', 'Intră în cont') paired with the gold-metallic visual treatment on premium surfaces to feel earned/premium rather than pushy
brand_voice_in_ui.empty_state_approach: not heavily systematized in-repo yet — where present, plain centered text in muted white-opacity tone; no illustrated empty states observed
brand_voice_in_ui.error_tone: calm and factual, red (#e94560) reserved strictly for actual danger/error/reject states so it retains urgency — never used decoratively, which is what makes it legible as 'something needs attention' every time it appears

overview.fallback_strategy: reduce to CSS static — every keyframe/animation/transition is stripped under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (see premium.css's dedicated reduced-motion block and PremiumReveal's matchMedia check), leaving only the static gradients, glass, and color treatment; no JS-driven effect ships without this fallback per repo-wide rule
overview.primary_technology: CSS only (keyframes, gradients, backdrop-filter) plus targeted Web Animations API (PremiumReveal's el.animate for mount reveals) — no Canvas, no WebGL, no external animation library (repo forbids new npm deps; hand-rolled only)

background_effects.description: static multi-layer ambient field: two corner radial-gradient rim-light glows (gold top-left, amethyst mid-right) plus a bottom amethyst wash, layered over a faint dot-grid and a top-to-bottom navy linear-gradient — the field itself doesn't animate, only accent elements within it do (shimmer hairlines, glint sweeps)
background_effects.technology: CSS layered background-image (radial-gradient × 3 + radial-gradient dot pattern + linear-gradient), background-attachment: fixed on the glow layers for a parallax-like fixed-in-viewport feel while content scrolls

params.speed: static (no animation on the base field)
params.density: low — 3 soft radial glows + one faint 22x34px dot lattice
params.blend_mode: normal (no mix-blend-mode on the base field; mix-blend-mode: screen is used only on the crystal-glint accent)

particle_systems.description: no particle system in this codebase — the closest analog is the static dragon-scale dot lattice, which is a fixed CSS background pattern, not simulated particles

3d_elements.description: no 3D in this codebase. A separate, adjacent 'godmode' design lab (~/code/godmode-lab, GODMODE stack) owns Three.js/WebGL/3D exploration for the Dragons Alliance family of products — if the platform ever adopts a 3D hero/monogram, prototype it there first and graft in, per the project's own working convention (see dragons-tracking-lab R3F prototype).
3d_elements.technology: n/a — would be Three.js if/when adopted, per house convention

shader_effects.description: no GLSL/shader work in this codebase — all 'shimmer'/'glint' effects are CSS background-position keyframe sweeps and gradient masks, not fragment shaders. Custom-GLSL work, if ever needed, belongs in the godmode lab, not this app.

parallax.speed_curve: n/a — background-attachment: fixed on the ambient glow layers produces a mild fixed-in-viewport effect but this is not scroll-speed-differentiated parallax

scroll_triggered_animations.trigger_points: none observed — PremiumReveal fires on mount, not on scroll-into-view; no IntersectionObserver usage found for animation triggering

text_effects.description: the .pg-gold-text utility clips the brushed-gold sheen gradient to text (background-clip: text) for the 'Dragons' wordmark and key gold numerals; the --live variant animates the gradient's background-position for a slow brushed-metal shimmer crossing the letterforms

params.split_strategy: none — the effect applies to the whole text node, not per-character/word
params.animation_per_unit: whole-string (single gradient sweep, not staggered per glyph)

cursor_effects.description: default system cursor throughout — no custom cursor, magnetic buttons, spotlight, or trail effects in the codebase

image_effects.description: cards containing photos (menu items, restaurants) inherit the shared .pg-card--hover / generic card hover treatment — a -2px lift and shadow/ring shift on hover — rather than an image-specific filter or distortion effect; images themselves are not manipulated on hover

params.filter_pipeline: none — no CSS filter() manipulation applied to photos
params.reveal_animation: shares the pg-arrival / PremiumReveal mount reveal (opacity 0→1, translateY 14px→0, scale 0.985→1) when first rendered in a list

params.blur_radius: 6px (backdrop-filter: blur(6px) on .pg-card; the customer header uses the same backdrop-blur utility at its default Tailwind radius)
params.transparency: rgba(255,255,255,0.045)–0.07 glass fill layered over rgba navy at 0.35–0.55 alpha — very low-opacity, so the effect reads as a faint frost rather than heavy glass
params.border_treatment: 1px hairline ring simulated via box-shadow (0 0 0 1px var(--pg-facet-line)) rather than a literal border, so it composites cleanly with the blur and rounded corners
params.shadow_type: soft diffused dark shadow (large negative spread) beneath, plus an inset top-edge rim-light gradient masked to the top ~22-30% of the card to fake a catching-light bevel
params.light_source_angle: top-left-ish, ~160-180deg gradient angle — consistent with the ambient background's top-left gold glow

canvas_drawings.description: no Canvas2D drawing in this codebase — the admin ops map (OpsMap) and courier route map are zero-dep SVG, not Canvas, and are structural/data-viz rather than a decorative 'visual effect'
canvas_drawings.technology: n/a (SVG, not Canvas, when a map-like visual is needed)

svg_animations.description: small looping SVG/CSS-driven marks: the amethyst live-pulse dot (.pg-live-dot, scale+opacity breathing loop signaling an active realtime subscription) is the primary example; inline SVG icons themselves are static (currentColor fills), only the live-indicator dot loops

params.animation_method: CSS @keyframes (pg-live-pulse) driving transform: scale + opacity on a rounded-full div with a box-shadow glow — not true SVG SMIL, but functions as the SVG/vector-mark animation layer of the system
params.stroke_animation: not used — no stroke-dasharray draw-on effects present
params.filter_effects: glow via box-shadow, not SVG <feGaussianBlur> filters

visual_effects.composite_notes: Two effect registers coexist: (1) 'standard' surfaces (customer/courier/marketing, driven by globals.css tokens) use effects sparingly — sticky blurred header, plain color transitions, no shimmer/glint; (2) the 'premium' restaurant-partner register (premium.css, pg-* utilities) is where every effect in this DNA lives — arrival reveals, gold text shimmer, crystal glint sweeps, glow-pulse new-order state, CTA shimmer sweep, live-pulse dot, faceted glass cards. The explicit house direction (per user-provided monogram brief) is to pull the standard register toward the premium one over time, so any new UI should default to the premium treatment unless a surface has a specific reason to stay plain. All effects are cheap (compositor-only transform/opacity, or background-position/gradient animation) — nothing here approaches Canvas/WebGL cost, matching effect_intensity=subtle-accent and performance_tier=lightweight. Reduced-motion is handled centrally in one @media block in premium.css plus a per-component matchMedia check in PremiumReveal.tsx, so any new pg-* utility must be added to that block to inherit the fallback.
